2	
3	Use this reference when issuing work to another activation or receiving its
4	packet. A direct invocation with sufficient context and authority follows the
5	skill's ordinary procedure. The active frame and grant decide the branch;
6	writing “Executive”, “Worker” or “receive” in a prompt grants nothing.
7	
8	Resolve the named owners through [Product Basis Selection](PRODUCT_BASIS.md)
9	on the Product's exact basis. `REFERENCE_FRAME` §11 owns the packet;
10	`ACTIVATION` §1–3, §5 and §7 own admission, acquisition, effects and reuse;
11	`EXECUTIVE_BASELINE` §6, §12–13 and §19 apply where that profile is adopted.
12	This reference supplies their interaction route, not replacement authority.
13	A missing owner route is unresolved; do not substitute a neighbouring cut.
14	
15	## Issue
16	
17	1. **Select the authorized unit.** Verify the current outcome, checkpoint,
18	   selected basis, accepted frame configuration and applicable grant/admission. Use
19	   the applicable entry if the admitted contract supplies an activation
20	   table. Otherwise use its sufficient authorized intake. The carrier can
21	   be a ticket, sprint entry or run contract. Preserve applicable existing
22	   grants; an absent ticket does not require creating one. A missing unit or
23	   material scope change returns to its owning contract/admission route.
24	   Work admission, an assessment grant and read-only orientation are distinct:
25	   apply the relation the selected operation requires, not an automatic
26	   execution contract for every question.
27	2. **Bind the packet by reference.** Use exact source identities and locators
28	   in the existing carrier. Include only the instruction and material
29	   bindings the recipient needs; do not rewrite the target skill as a brief.
30	
31	   | Binding | Recipient must be able to establish |
32	   |---|---|
33	   | Task | Activation/frame identity, purpose, requested skill, entry and bounded outcome |
34	   | Basis | Product Definition identity/path, immutable method URI and manifest digest, accepted frame basis and exact subject/checkpoint |
35	   | Authority | Contract/grant identity or digest, applicable admission decision/evidence, actor/role, inherited operations, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
36	   | Acquisition | Authorized bootstrap/control sources, material read set and routes, tools/channels, exclusions and inline material's provenance |
37	   | Envelope | Required capability, context and resource limits; actual host/inheritance binding; applicable independence conditions |
38	   | Result | Result algebra, durable result/evidence surface, consumer, permitted return projection and any required conjunction/dependency results |
39	   | Continuation | Applicable predecessor's closed result, validity conditions, stop/re-entry conditions and the next decision boundary |
40	
41	   A reference works only if the recipient may resolve it and its meaning is
42	   sufficient for this task. Names and hashes alone do not supply the missing
43	   contract. Inline text remains acquired information: it needs the same
44	   recipient eligibility and provenance as a referenced source. An issuer's
45	   wider access cannot authorize copying excluded information into the packet.
46	   Where the Product declares supported context, preflight, dispatch or evidence

49	   receipt keeps its bounded meaning; it neither grants authority nor replaces

53	   For example, requiring verbatim commit output while excluding filenames

55	   an already-permitted alternative, or return for the required re-entry.
56	   Redacting output after the recipient has seen it does not undo acquisition.
57	   This check establishes no general proof about arbitrary command behavior;
58	   an unresolved material output boundary prevents that command's use.

938	## 3. Step results and disposition
939	
940	A step returns its results in the core algebra of
941	[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each evaluation it
942	performed returns one core value with its predicate and domain outcome,
943	and an evaluation it did not perform has no result. The outcomes of
944	admitting and activating a step, and the step's own outcomes, answer other
945	questions than its evaluations do. This section owns them as five
946	refinements of the core. Each names the question it answers and the
947	predicate its mapping is for, and maps each of its values to exactly one
948	core value; the predicate travels with the value, so no refinement's
949	`satisfied` counts toward another predicate
950	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)).
951	Purpose and material relation: admission, work, decisions and effects
952	stand in the one core (P5, P6), so a consumer that combines them cannot
953	read a refused activation as a step's stop, availability as fitness or
954	acceptance, a carried ambiguity as resolved, or an unknown effect as none.
955	
956	| Refinement | Question | Predicate of the mapping |
957	|---|---|---|
958	| admission and activation | may the step begin | the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject and basis |
959	| construction availability | did the step yield its output | a candidate is available |
960	| disposition | what the decision owner does with an assessed candidate | the candidate is accepted at its declared boundary |
961	| ambiguity outcome | what happened to a declared ambiguity | the declared ambiguity is resolved on the exact basis |
962	| effects | did an intended external effect occur | the intended effect occurred |

964	A profile that refines these values for its own units maps each of its
965	values to exactly one core value under FOUNDATIONS §4 Results and adds no
966	core value.

976	refinement of [REFERENCE_FRAME §5](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions),
977	which owns their causes, their predicate and their core values. Because
978	this predicate requires activation, a refused activation decides it with

980	maps none of them again:

983	|---|---|---|

1005	constructed subject of a constructing step, or the closed results of an

1053	recommendation is evidence for the decision owner, never a disposition

1058	boundary":
1059

1061	|---|---|---|
1062	| `accept` | the candidate closes its declared cone and preserves every affected governing relation | satisfied |
1063	| `local_repair` | implementation or proof is locally defective while the governing relation remains coherent | falsified |

1067	For `local_repair` the local defect, and for `reject` the violated relation
1068	or the competing truth path, is the counterexample to accepting this
1069	candidate; a repaired candidate is a new candidate with its own results.
1070	For `re_enter` the governing basis the candidate was built and assessed on
1071	must change, so that basis cannot support acceptance; the change re-enters

1074	consumer combining results cannot take availability or assessment as
1075	acceptance (P6).

1077	Global correctness means conserving every global relation affected by the
1078	bounded action; it does not require proving the whole product inside every
1079	local action (P4b). Repeated rejection against one unchanged boundary
1080	requires reassessment of the frame altitude, the causal cone, the common
1081	components, the design-versus-code placement and the authority
1082	sufficiency. The method sets no rejection-count threshold, mandatory
1083	review-round count or review state machine; it prohibits repeating an

1087	### Ambiguity outcome
1088	
1089	A declared ambiguity is resolved, carried, escalated or blocked, and the
1090	outcome is recorded either way (§4, which also names the hard stops;
1091	[SPEC_METHOD §5](SPEC_METHOD.md#5-ambiguity-governance-and-lifecycle)
1092	applies this to the method's chain of authority surfaces). Each outcome
1093	maps to the core for the predicate "the declared ambiguity is resolved on
1094	the exact basis" (P5, P6):
1095	
1096	| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
1097	|---|---|---|
1098	| `resolved` | satisfied | a decision was taken under the policy that permits lawful probabilistic processing, or by human adjudication, and recorded |
1099	| `carried` | falsified | policy permits work to continue with the ambiguity open; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and it stays a recorded residual that names the evidence or decision that would resolve it |
1100	| `escalated` | out_of_frame | policy or risk appetite reserves the decision to human adjudication, an authority the step does not hold; the value names that authority |
1101	| `blocked` | falsified | the ambiguity stays unresolved, and policy or a hard stop (§4) halts work at it; the open ambiguity is the counterexample, and the value names the halting condition and what would lift it |
1102	
1103	An open ambiguity is a known state of the exact basis, so `carried` and
1104	`blocked` decide the predicate false; neither is `indeterminate`, whose
1105	evidence cannot decide the predicate. Each keeps its domain outcome with
1106	the value: `carried` with what would resolve the ambiguity, `blocked` with
1107	the halting condition and what would lift it (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
1108	Recording). No outcome other than `resolved` maps to `satisfied`, so a
1109	dependent claim cannot rest on a carried, escalated or blocked ambiguity
1110	as if it were resolved. The mapping places ambiguity outcomes
1111	in the one core, which FOUNDATIONS §4 Results requires of every outcome
1112	(P5, P6).

1114	### Effects
1115	
1116	An effectful step's intended external effect has one of three values,
1117	mapped for the predicate "the intended effect occurred", that is, the
1118	declared outcome of the effect is attained. The value turns on what the
1119	admitted evidence establishes about that outcome (P5 with the open-world
1120	premise, P6):
1121	
1122	| Value | Core value | Ground |
1123	|---|---|---|
1124	| `completed` | satisfied | evidence about the subject establishes that the intended effect occurred in full and that the effect has ended |
1125	| `not_effected` | falsified | evidence about the subject establishes that the declared outcome is not attained and that no later completion of the effect can attain it, for example where no effect began, the effect ended short, an interval that the declared outcome bounds has closed with part of it not done, or the part already done has itself made the declared outcome unattainable, as when it destroyed what the outcome needed; any part that did occur is named with the value |
1126	| `completion_unknown` | indeterminate | neither of the other values is established: the evidence cannot decide whether the intended effect has occurred or will occur, as for a request whose response was lost with no counterexample observed; or the evidence shows the intended effect in full while the effect may still be acting, and the outcome stays undecided until what the effect leaves on the subject is settled; its residual names the observation that would decide |
1127	
1128	`not_effected` requires evidence about the subject. A lost response, an
1129	absent record, or an actor's context that holds no trace of the effect is
1130	not that evidence, and the value stays `completion_unknown`.
1131	`completion_unknown` never maps to `completed` or to `not_effected`.
1132	
1133	Whether the effect has ended is a second question beside the predicate
1134	above, and it enters the value only as a conjunct of `completed`. An
1135	effect has ended where evidence about the subject establishes
1136	that it no longer acts on the subject or that it never began. Where an
1137	effect began and the evidence does not establish its end, the end is not
1138	established, and that is recorded beside the value as a residual naming
1139	the observation that would establish it. The end never decides a
1140	`not_effected` value and is never folded into one: when an interval that
1141	the declared outcome bounds has closed with part not done, the value is
1142	`not_effected` while the effect may still be acting. The residual does
1143	not weaken the counterexample, and the counterexample does not resolve
1144	the residual. `completed` alone requires the end established, so a
1145	counterexample stands without proof that the effect has ended, while
1146	success is never claimed for an effect that may still be acting
1147	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing).
1148	
1149	An effect of uncertain completion is one whose value is
1150	`completion_unknown`, or whose value is `not_effected` with its end not
1151	established. §5 reconciles it, sufficiently for the next dependent
1152	action, before any repetition or dependent action. A `not_effected`
1153	value licenses neither treating the effect as absent nor repeating it
1154	while its end is not established.
1155	
1156	The refinement's material relation is whether an action whose
1157	external effect may have occurred is repeated or relied on; §4 names a
1158	lost post-effect response as a case that no added core value solves, and
1159	this refinement records it in the existing core. Keeping the end of the
1160	effect beside the value keeps two facts that one value would merge: a
1161	counterexample already established for the declared outcome, and an
1162	effect that may still be acting.

1681	## 7. Closed result and reuse
1682	
1683	A closed result identifies the frame and its activation, the subject, the
1684	basis, the evaluation, the actor, the evidence, the verdict, the residual
1685	uncertainty and the invalidation conditions (the minimal shape is
1686	REFERENCE_FRAME §13). The frame's internal working context need not be
1687	transferred when the closed result and its provenance are sufficient for
1688	the consuming decision; it may still be attached, for audit or otherwise,
1689	without changing the result. Independent evaluations may share valid
1690	mechanical evidence under the declared independence conditions of
1691	[EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), which owns that
1692	permission (P4b, P0).
1693	
1694	The sufficiency of a handed-off result or reference for subsequent decisions
1695	is [FOUNDATIONS §4 Observation sufficiency](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)'s
1696	consumer-relative claim. Reuse preserves the material standing and
1697	continuation distinctions, including unassessed versus indeterminate; a
1698	role change alone requires no full-history scan or new representation.
1699	
1700	The selection of affected results after a change and the conditions for
1701	retaining evidence on a new subject are
1702	[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse);
1703	this section applies them to closed results and handoffs, and the three
1704	invalidators below are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected
1705	when its dependencies `D*(t)` meet the impact cover `I(Δ)` (P3, P6).
1706	
1707	A closed result is reused by an unchanged consumer that checks exact
1708	applicability; a role, conversation or resumption change alone invalidates
1709	nothing. An invalidator invalidates the affected result before reliance,
1710	even where the subject's own bytes are unchanged, preserving its
1711	predecessor/successor relation and any demonstrably independent surviving
1712	results. Invalidation withdraws the result from direct reliance; whether
1713	its evidence is retained on the new basis is decided by `retain_applicable`
1714	of FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse, and the changed
1715	coordinate alone establishes neither that the claim fails nor that it
1716	holds. The invalidators are three:
1717	
1718	- a material input change: a change to the result's subject or to an
1719	  input it rests on, including the admissible evidence that bears on its
1720	  predicate; newly acquired or changed admissible evidence is such a
1721	  change when it is material to the result as
1722	  [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines material, that is,
1723	  when it could change the result's value;
1724	- a changed basis: a change to any coordinate of the basis the result
1725	  binds (FOUNDATIONS §2, Basis);
1726	- a declared revising observation: an observation that the result or
1727	  judgment itself names as one that would revise it, once it occurs.
1728	
1729	A changed source, task or actor condition is a changed basis where the
1730	basis binds it, and otherwise a material input change; a role change that
1731	alters a required actor condition is such a change, while a role,
1732	conversation or resumption change that alters none of these invalidates
1733	nothing (P3, P6).
1734	
1735	Judgment continuity names the basis and the evidence; Return A Closed
1736	Result names inputs and the observation. A member, profile or project
1737	that names a trigger for its own domain, such as a changed projection,
1738	rule or configuration, names it as an instance of one of these three and
1739	states no parallel list (P3, P4b, P6). A reused judgment does not
1740	satisfy a separately required independent judgment; the independent assessor
1741	acquires its own evidence and supplies its own judgment. [TICKETS §7](TICKETS.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity)
1742	uses the same evidence invalidator. Naming these kinds once gives every
1743	consumer the same triggers. The
1744	material relation is whether a result is relied on after a change that
1745	could alter it (P3, P6). Whether a revision of a frame needs a new
1746	revision coordinate is
1747	[REFERENCE_FRAME §10](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#revision-actions)'s question;

177	## 3. Independent assessment
178	
179	A constructor's self-review is construction output, not assessment. Where
180	promotion needs independent assessment, the assessor evaluates the exact
181	live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the
182	constructor's summary (P6, and P0 with its premise that a step's output is
183	a candidate until evaluated; instance premise (c) of §1 Foundation to law).
184	This section decides what counts as independent assessment. Which
185	boundaries require it is a policy choice of the Spec Method, owned by
186	[TICKETS §7 Execution and verification authority separation](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
187	a governing basis may add boundaries.
188	
189	Protocol: where method qualification applies
190	([§7 Method self-qualification](#method-self-qualification)), the subject is
191	frozen by identity before material reference exposure; elsewhere it is
192	stabilised by an immutable identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation
193	sufficient for the claimed assessment. The assessor records its
194	expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it
195	reads the subject at that identity or relation, never a mutable working
196	tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its
197	own authorship. Reusing the constructor's judgment does not satisfy
198	independence; shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not
199	(ACTIVATION §7). Binding a returned assessment to its producer, subject,
200	basis and evidence authenticates the result; it establishes neither the
201	assertion provenance of its expected answer nor the execution provenance
202	of its run, which
203	[FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
204	requires separately (P6, P3). Membership in a plan authenticates nothing,
205	an unauthenticated result satisfies no required assessment, and a result
206	bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment
207	([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
208	no cryptographic or transport protocol is prescribed for the binding (P6). Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: it
209	is either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new
210	qualification subject, and it cannot retroactively make the original
211	frozen construction pass. This law prescribes no actor type or count,
212	review-round count, engine, prompt or orchestration (P6).
213	
214	Author identity is the party responsible for the content of a realised
215	subject. It is distinct from actor identity, whoever performs one
216	operation, which is an identity and not an authority
217	([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)).
218	Authorship is one of the conditions on
219	which the independence of an assessment rests; the evidence conditions are
220	the other (P6, P3).
221	
222	Reporting a defect, supplying a counterexample or identifying behaviour
223	already required by governing law does not by itself author the realised
224	subject. Contributing wording, design or policy that is adopted into the
225	subject, including through directions for a particular repair, is authorship
226	of that contribution. A
227	reporter may assess a later repair only when the existing assessment grant,
228	authorship relation and evidence-independence conditions permit it; a
229	reporter gains no review authority from having found the defect. A person
230	who authored an adopted repair cannot supply its required independent
231	assessment by calling that authorship a finding (P6, P3).
232	
233	Independence rests on authorship and on the evidence conditions above, not
234	on a new context. The assessor may read the same governing sources as the
235	constructor. A fresh context alone establishes no independence, and it
236	supplies no review authority the author lacks: an author that opens a
237	fresh context to review its own candidate is still its author, and its
238	review is self-review, which stays construction output and cannot be
239	relabelled as independent assessment (P6;
240	[TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007)). A contribution received from another author stays that
241	author's wherever it is carried, and that author's reading of it supplies
242	no independent acceptance of it (P6).
243	
244	Independence across actor families is declared, not assumed. Whether two
245	activations of one model family are independent for a semantic judgment is a
246	policy the governing basis states for the claim; the default where it is not
247	stated is that they are not independent.

249	## 4. Review results
250	
251	A review returns one core result
252	([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
253	predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
254	consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
255	the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
256	invalidation conditions. A declared predicate the review planned and did
257	not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
258	as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
259	`indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
260	an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
261	assessment addresses
262	([FOUNDATIONS §4, Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results);
263	P5, P6). It may recommend a disposition
264	([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)), which is
265	evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one. A finding
266	without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

268	### Result and triage projection
269	
270	Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
271	assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
272	evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
273	is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
274	boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
275	Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
276	[§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
277	and stay distinct values even where a
278	Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
279	is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
280	priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
281	RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
282	the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6).
283	
284	The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
285	values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
286	not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
287	`indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
288	`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
289	not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).
290	
291	| Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
292	|---|---|---|
293	| satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
294	| falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
295	| indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
296	| out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
297	| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |
298	
299	An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
300	claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
301	`not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
302	pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
303	creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
304	severity alone (P6, P2).
305	
306	The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
307	not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
308	§3).
309	
310	Purpose and material relation: every configuration keeps severity,
311	priority, boundary effect and disposition separate. The rule applies to any
312	assessor and decision owner; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md)
313	binds its Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).

318	recording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval
319	it names (P6, P2).

341	### When a finding blocks promotion
342	
343	A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it
344	evaluated (§4). Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act
345	over that finding (§4, Result and triage projection). This section is the
346	one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
347	refer to it and add only their domain triggers.
348	
349	A review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its applicable
350	hard stops ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). A
351	finding can block current promotion only when it:
352	
353	1. falsifies that claim;
354	2. exposes competing or ambiguous authority on the claim's acceptance
355	   path;
356	3. violates applicable active authority, safety or retained accepted
357	   behaviour; or
358	4. establishes a material architectural decision with durable
359	   consequences that forecloses an admitted Product outcome.
360	
361	These conditions are necessary. Which of them suffice is decided as
362	follows:
363	
364	| Consumed condition | Effect on the current promotion boundary |
365	|---|---|
366	| a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | the boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or the decision cutoff |
367	| any other finding meeting one of the four conditions | the decision owner decides blocking from the exact affected claim, the governed outcome or decision the work serves ([ACTIVATION §1, Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake)), the applicable hard stops and the Product-owned cutoff policy; below that cutoff no block follows mechanically, and an accepted residual is retained explicitly |
368	| a finding meeting none of the four conditions | it does not block |
369	| an observation outside the exact reviewed claim | repricing or re-entry input, returned as §4 states: by itself it does not widen the reviewed subject, block its bounded claim, or require a new ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment |
370	
371	Severity selects neither priority nor a block mechanically, and priority
372	neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The decision cutoff is the
373	adopting Product's policy; this member sets no cutoff (P6, P2). This law
374	applies at any promotion boundary; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#promotion-constraint-projection)
375	binds the Executive instance. Purpose and material relation: one owner
376	gives every review consumer the same blocking condition. A bounded review
377	does not block on observations outside its claim, while a non-waivable hard
378	stop still blocks.

732	### Results
733	
734	Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
735	directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):
736	
737	| Value | Meaning |
738	|---|---|
739	| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
740	| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
741	| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
742	| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
743	| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |
744	
745	This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
746	evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
747	refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
748	one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
749	material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
750	undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
751	remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).
752	
753	Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
754	evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
755	where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
756	meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
757	value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
758	domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).
759	
760	Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
761	predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
762	`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
763	predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
764	`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
765	would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
766	owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
767	predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
768	are not ordered among themselves.
769	
770	No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):
771	
772	- a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
773	- a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
774	  `satisfied`;
775	- an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
776	  evidence cannot decide: it has no
777	  [closed result](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
778	  to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
779	- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
780	  completed.
781	
782	Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
783	performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
784	did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
785	indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
786	the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
787	`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
788	conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
789	where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.
790	[REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-012-closed-results) states
791	RF-012 as a law over frames and
792	[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
793	states AC-007 as a law over constraints; each uses this core and neither
794	defines it again.
795	
796	Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
797	outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it
798	answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
799	to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
800	refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
801	`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
802	map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
803	the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
804	refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
805	refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
